title: CFDE Webinar Series
bodyHtml:
The NIH Common Fund Data Ecosystem (CFDE) is a network of programs conducting innovative, cross-domain research to benefit human health. This CFDE Webinar Series brings the varied programs of the CFDE to the broad biomedical research community. Join us on the last Friday of each month at 1-2 PM ET to learn the science behind the research programs that comprise CFDE, as well as about the CFDE as a whole and its coordination Centers.

Join us on Friday, September 25th, 2026 for our next session of the Public Webinar Series!

? From Genes to Mechanisms: AI-Assisted Discovery across the Data Distillery Knowledge Graph

? Attendees will learn how to:

  1. Connect genetics to biology: Trace genes, regulatory variants, phenotypes, and disease associations across pathways, tissues, cellular contexts, and model-organism evidence using the Data Distillery Knowledge Graph (DDKG).
  2. Ask biological questions more easily: See how ddkg.skill enables general-purpose AI assistants to translate research questions into reproducible DDKG graph queries—without requiring deep knowledge of the graph’s underlying structure.
  3. Move toward testable mechanisms: Learn how integrated biomedical evidence and AI-assisted exploration can help researchers move beyond genetic associations to identify candidate pathways, biological mechanisms, and hypotheses for further investigation.

August 30th, 2024

Acute to Chronic Pain Signatures – an initiative to identify biomarkers and advance pain science

Dr. Martin Lundquist of Johns Hopkins School of Public Health, Dr. Ari Kahn of The University of Texas at Austin, and Seth Berke of Johns Hopkins School of Public Health.

Chronic pain impacts over 50 million Americans, yet current treatments often fall short due to limited understanding of its mechanisms. Pain biomarkers hold significant promise for revealing biological pathways and phenotypical changes associated with pain, offering possible targets for treatment and aiding in the early identification of patients who might benefit from early intervention. While biomarkers are currently used for diagnosing, monitoring, and treating other diseases, there are currently no validated clinical biomarkers for chronic pain. To address this issue, the National Institutes of Health (NIH) Common Fund initiated the Acute to Chronic Pain Signatures (A2CPS) program, which aims to assess and develop potential biomarkers into biosignatures and discover new ones related to the transition from acute to chronic pain following surgery. In this talk we will discuss the goals of A2CPS, including a description of the datatypes collected and how to access data. We will also discuss how a new researcher may go about accessing Common Fund resources, such as the data that will be released by A2CPS, to investigate a novel scientific inquiry utilizing cloud platforms and other tools made available to the CFDE.
